objectives.text: Turn the Association Agreement with the EU into a single-market deal without full membership. The Council authorised its signing on 16 July 2026, signing is expected in late September 2026, the European Parliament must still consent, and the government has promised a referendum on a text that polls split almost evenly. The EU is the only route to market access beyond the two neighbours.

objectives.text: Keep the co-principality and the two neighbours as the frame of the state. The French president and the Bishop of Urgell share the head of state under the constitution, and France and Spain are the only land routes in and out. Security, mobility and visas are run with them: the 2003 Franco-Spanish-Andorran convention coordinates visa and residence rules, and in June 2026 Andorra signed a 2026-2030 work plan with Catalonia on airport hours and mobility.

objectives.text: Keep the tourism economy: duty-free shopping, low taxes and winter and summer resorts. UNWTO data put tourism at 71.8 percent of GDP, the highest share in its ranking, which makes the model a dependency as much as a means. Banking, the third pillar, is now under EU and US pressure and cannot be the only growth engine.

means.text: Customs union with the EU since 1 July 1991, which treats manufactured goods as inside the union, and the euro as currency under a monetary agreement signed in 2011 and in force since 2012, with Andorran euro coins issued from 2015. Both are the instruments that let a state without its own currency or tariffs trade and sell.

means.text: Multilateral presence far above its size: a full UN member since 1993, with the Council of Europe and the OSCE as its European forums. It buys visibility with small voluntary contributions, such as EUR 10,000 to the Council of Europe Action Plan for Ukraine signed in June 2025, and with humanitarian grants routed through international agencies.

means.text: No armed forces, as Andorra's own report to the UN records. Security is delegated in practice to the two neighbours that are its co-princes: France and Spain are the only land entry points, and Andorra has no military capacity of its own to defend its borders.

constraints.text: No armed forces, and no fixed-wing airport inside the territory. Access is by road or helicopter through France or Spain, and the nearest commercial airport is La Seu d'Urgell in Catalonia, owned by the Catalan government. A state that depends on its neighbours for air access and for security has little room to act without them.

constraints.text: No route into the EEA. Membership is open only to EU and EFTA members, and the Commission's 2013 report judged small-state participation not viable at present. The single-market access that Liechtenstein has through the EEA must therefore come from a bilateral Association Agreement, which is slower and still unratified.

In March 2015 FinCEN named Banca Privada d'Andorra a money-laundering concern, Andorran authorities took the bank over, and its Spanish unit went bankrupt; S&P then downgraded Andorra. paradoxes.text: Low taxes and duty-free sales built the state, and the EU deal and US pressure ask it to shrink exactly those advantages. The BPA affair showed that one bank's tax-haven clients can cost the whole financial sector its correspondent access, which is why the Association Agreement, meant to secure market access, forces the sector to open its books.

grand_strategy.reading: Andorra borrows its security and its mobility from the two neighbours that are also its co-princes, and sells tourism and duty-free shopping inside a customs union with the EU. Its structural problem is that the banking side, which paid for much of the state, now has to meet EU and US standards to keep market access, and the Association Agreement is the price of that access. Monaco stalled in 2023 while Andorra and San Marino went on, so the microstate track is not a fixed club; the 2026 signature and the referendum that follows are the test.

stances.note: Treaty-based: the 1993 Treaty of Good Neighbourliness, Friendship and Cooperation with Spain and France, and the constitution that makes the French president one of the two co-princes. The co-princely link is older (the 1607 edict, the 1278 pareatge), but the 1993 treaty is the standing legal tie, so since is 1993. France and Andorra have had diplomatic relations since 3 June 1993. Bond - affinity: a shared Romance-language and cultural space and a long habit of co-sovereignty, not kinship. The French co-prince holds the office by virtue of being president of France; Andorran voters do not choose either co-prince.

stances.note: Treaty-based, same 1993 treaty as France, and the second co-prince is the Bishop of Urgell, a Spanish see in Catalonia. Spain supplies about 58 percent of Andorran imports (2025). Bond - kin: the Andorran people are descended from the Catalans and Catalan is the only official language, so the bond is shared identity, not just interest. Grade follows the structure, not the rhetoric: the Catalan government signs its own 2026-2030 plan with Andorra, which is a sub-state tie, not a Madrid one.

stances.note: The EU is partner for a non-member, under the ontology, even though Andorra is inside the customs union for manufactured goods since 1 July 1991. The 2026 Council authorisation to sign the Association Agreement is the warming: the agreement is the aim, not membership, which the government has not sought. Bond - none: interest-based cooperation, no kinship or grievance in the sources. The trend is warming because the signing is scheduled for late September 2026, but the European Parliament and a referendum still stand between text and law.

stances.note: Andorra aligns with EU Russia sanctions by government decree, since 2022: the 22 May 2026 decree brings in the EU 19th and 20th packages, with annexes of 2,469 individuals and 1,636 entities. No source calls Russia a rival, and Andorra does not seek Russia's defeat or regime change, so adversary does not apply. The grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C): sanctions are applied against a state whose clients have laundered money through Andorran banks (the 2015 BPA case, with Russian criminal clients named by FinCEN), and the financial centre must now isolate them. Bond - none.
